description: Gemma4-31B chunked prefill on a BH Galaxy, 60 layers = 50 local + 10 global. BLINDED: harness description only, no results.

legality.note: sliding_halo_hop_count = ceil(window/(chunk/cp)) must be <= cp; window=1024, cp=8 -> floor is chunk>=1024 (models/demos/gemma4_d_p/tt/model.py:152)

e2e.summary_re: \[traced_perf\] DEVICE (?P<tokens>\d+) tokens in (?P<device_s>[0-9.]+)s \((?P<tok_s>\d+) tok/s\) \| staging (?P<staging_s>[0-9.]+)s \| readback (?P<readback_s>[0-9.]+)s

layer_bench.result_re: \[layer_perf_chunk\] RESULT type=(?P<lt>\w+) chunk=(?P<idx>\d+) ring_depth=\d+ kv_actual_global=(?P<kv>\d+) measured_ms=(?P<ms>[0-9.]+)

layer_count_override.reason: no env knob; num_hidden_layers is read from the HF config and validate_31b_config() (tt/model_config.py) hard-rejects a changed value. Layer-count differencing needs a temporary patch -> assisted path only.

ablation_catalogue.scope_note: halves bytes but not tile count, so it refutes byte-bandwidth, not per-tile overhead

ablation_sites_note: These env vars are DIAGNOSTIC PATCHES, not in-tree. Each needs a temporary edit to the site listed. Level 3 is assisted only: propose, get approval, verify the revert with `git diff --stat` against a recorded pre-patch sha.

artifacts._: populate as this investigation produces captures; nothing is pre-supplied.

_BLINDED: This profile deliberately carries NO results. It is the harness description a session
would have for a model nobody has investigated yet: how to run the tests, what the
layer types are, and the work-unit math read out of the op's source.
Removed relative to gemma4.json, because each would hand the session a conclusion:
validation{}            the a/slope table, the 12 per-op rows, the 4 headline results
artifacts.captures{}    the six captures and their prior-context design
artifacts.*_logs        the e2e, depth-curve and layer-count logs already on disk
layers.types[].note     free-text that stated which layer owns which term
growing_op.name         naming the op that grows IS headline result #1
Kept, because it is description and not result:
occupancy_model.occupancy  the div_up work-unit math, readable from
ring_joint_sdpa_program_factory.cpp. It says how the op DIVIDES work, not what
that costs. It is applied to whichever op the subtraction shows growing.
`ppd.py validate --profile gemma4-blind` will refuse: there is nothing to regress
against. That is the point. Use --profile gemma4 for the regression test.

occupancy_model._: work-unit math read from the program factory, for whichever op the measurement shows growing with context. Describes how work is divided, not what it costs.

occupancy.note: units = B*NH*ceil((chunk/cp)/q_chunk); depth = ceil(units/grid); cores with no unit run padded handshake iterations, so Cores always reads ~114
